newsitem.title: EGYPT: Dollar shortage pushes Egyptian pound down.
newsitem.headline: Dollar shortage pushes Egyptian pound down.

text.p: A shortage in U.S. dollars in the Egyptian private-sector money market on Sunday helped push the Egyptian pound down, bankers said.
They said public-sector banks continued to siphon the U.S. currency from the market as June 30, the end of their financial year, loomed.
Private-sector bankers said the dollar ranged from 3.3955 pounds to 3.3975 pounds bid and from 3.3965 pounds to 3.3995 offered in the interbank market.
A survey of four actively trading banks gave average rates of 3.3964 pounds bid and 3.3978 pounds offered. These averages compared to 3.3955 pounds bid and 3.3975 offered on Thursday.
The Central Bank calculated the average exchange rate at closing as 3.399764 buy and 3.397249 sell.
